question: The volume (in cm³) of a wire of diameter 14 cm and length 12 m is: Take π=(22)/(7)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of **cylindrical wire** = πr²h

Convert **Length** to cm: 12 m = 1200 cm.

Radius (r) = Diameter ÷ 2 = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm.

Volume = (22/7) × 7 × 7 × 1200 = 154 × 1200 = 1,84,800 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 1,84,800 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Diameter** of wire = 14 cm

**Length (Height)** of wire = 12 m

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cylinder = πr²h

1 m = 100 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/941e207060ee9c5b8d3901948e516ff0932373c89d4fbd2edf1c6d5255705fb2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius (r) = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm

⇒ Height (h) = 12 × 100 = 1200 cm

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 7² × 1200

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 49 × 1200

⇒ Volume = 22 × 7 × 1200

⇒ Volume = 154 × 1200

⇒ Volume = 1,84,800 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1,84,800 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The total area including the curved surface and two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the side surface of the cylinder: CSA = 2πrh.

Unit Conversion

1 m³ = 10,00,000 cm³ and 1 liter = 1000 cm³.</p
